## Resolution

- **Issue:** #16 — `feat: implement audited needs-human PR remediation lifecycle`
- **Scope:** Implement the retained remediation lifecycle on the existing needs-human PR/branch, including authoritative finding inputs, deterministic classification, bounded fixes, fresh re-review, idempotent markers, and recovery tests.
- **Integration Base:** `dogfood` at `76bf6057d0c5f968a1eb86d873e07c208c3fc3e7`
- **Contract Status:** Resolved for investigation and implementation in the assigned worktree.

<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

- **Verdict:** CONFIRMED
- **Confidence:** High
- **Severity:** High
- **Task Type:** Workflow lifecycle and recovery

### What Was Claimed

Review-blocked pull requests currently become terminal lanes. The retained remediation contract requires recovery on the existing PR and branch, authoritative standalone finding issues, bounded classification and fixes, finding closure, fresh full review, guarded auto-land, durable progress markers, and crash-safe single-attempt semantics.

### What We Found

The Pi-native work-on path already publishes review-finding issues and has a basic in-memory `remediationAttempts` resume path in `src/workflows/work-on.ts`. That path is incomplete: it trusts the result payload rather than reloading authoritative finding issues, treats all confirmed/likely findings as mechanically fixable, does not transition the issue back to `workflow:in-review`, does not durably recover an already-started attempt from PR/issue markers, and closes findings without recording the remediation commit or verifying that only addressed findings were closed. The existing PR/branch is otherwise available through `findPullRequest` and the child resume binding.

### Root Cause

Remediation was modeled as a one-off child resume in the controller rather than as an idempotent, marker-backed lifecycle with deterministic classification and explicit finding issue state transitions. `ActiveRunLink.remediationAttempts` is session persistence only; GitHub artifacts are not consulted before dispatch. Finding publication also lacks a reusable authoritative-input loader and closure contract.

### Affected Files

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — remediation dispatch, classification, marker recovery, finding closure, and lifecycle artifacts.
- `src/adapters/github-workflow.ts` — issue comment/read-back and finding issue state operations needed by remediation.
- `test/workflows/review-findings.test.ts` — authoritative finding classification, closure, and idempotent recovery coverage.
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` — pure remediation policy and marker behavior coverage.

### Evidence

- `#attemptRemediation` filters only `confirmed`/`likely` findings from the child result and does not inspect standalone issue bodies beyond publication.
- No `workflow:in-review` label transition occurs when remediation begins.
- `remediationAttempts` is restored from session entries only; no existing `FORGE:REMEDIATION` marker is read before starting another attempt.
- Finding closure comments do not include a remediation commit identity and closure is based only on disappearance from the next result.
- `postRemediationArtifact` emits progress but cannot distinguish a recovered in-progress attempt from a completed attempt.

### History Findings

The repository contains the current Pi-native review gate and finding publication tests, but no durable remediation state model or remediation-specific test suite. Existing GitHub adapters already provide idempotent comment posting, issue reads, and close read-back primitives.

### Recommendation

Implement a bounded remediation coordinator around the existing PR/branch: parse and deduplicate linked `review-finding` issues, classify only contract-safe findings as fixable, leave policy/product/security-authority blockers open, transition the source issue to `workflow:in-review`, use deterministic attempt markers on both PR and issue, resume only the existing child/branch, close only findings proven absent after the remediation commit with commit evidence, and emit a completion marker for clean re-review or re-escalation. Add focused pure/helper tests for auto-land readiness, re-escalation, unfixable policy blocks, partial recovery, and closure.

### Related Issues

- Issue #16 — audited needs-human PR remediation lifecycle.
- Existing review-finding publication and review-gate behavior in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` and `src/core/review.ts`.

### Decomposition Assessment

Single bounded workflow concern. No decomposition is required; implementation remains in the existing work-on controller and adapter seam with focused tests.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Existing needs-human PR and branch are reused; no replacement PR or issue reset is created.
- [ ] Open linked `review-finding` issues are authoritative remediation inputs and are deduplicated.
- [ ] Fixable and unfixable/policy blockers are deterministic and separately reported.
- [ ] Fixable remediation transitions the source issue to `workflow:in-review`, runs one bounded fix/review cycle, and preserves unresolved finding issues.
- [ ] Addressed finding issues close with the remediation commit identity and only after fresh review.
- [ ] Clean non-main integration re-review remains eligible for parent-owned auto-land; protected main remains human-gated.
- [ ] PR and issue markers make start/completion idempotent and recoverable after partial failure.
- [ ] Tests cover auto-land, re-escalation, unfixable policy blocks, partial recovery, and finding closure.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### In Scope

- Reuse the existing needs-human PR and bound branch; never reset the issue or create a replacement PR.
- Treat open standalone `review-finding` issues linked to the PR as authoritative remediation inputs, with deterministic deduplication by PR/finding identity.
- Parse and classify findings into contract-safe mechanical fixes versus policy/product/security-authority escalation. Only confirmed or likely, non-policy findings are eligible for one bounded remediation attempt.
- Make remediation idempotent across PR and source-issue markers, recover an interrupted attempt, transition the source issue to `workflow:in-review`, and resume the existing work-on child/branch.
- Require a fresh full review before closing addressed finding issues or allowing the existing parent-owned merge/auto-land gate to proceed.
- Close only findings absent from the fresh review, after a changed remediation head is confirmed; include the remediation commit/head in the closure evidence. Leave unresolved and policy findings open.
- Emit durable `FORGE:REMEDIATION` progress and `FORGE:REMEDIATION:COMPLETE` re-escalation/clean-review artifacts on both PR and source issue.
- Add focused tests for classification, authoritative issue deduplication, partial marker recovery, finding closure evidence, re-escalation, and non-main auto-land eligibility through existing policy/gate behavior.

### Out of Scope

- New PRs, branch resets, direct merges, protected-branch policy changes, reviewer authority changes, or GitHub CI policy changes.
- Automatic remediation of product, UX, scope, billing, production-safety, insufficient-confidence, or explicit security-authority decisions.
- Changes to the public work-on result schema or the parent-owned merge/close/cleanup phases.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Existing PR/branch is reused for remediation.
- [ ] Linked open finding issues are authoritative and deduplicated.
- [ ] Fixable/unfixable classification is deterministic and reported.
- [ ] Start markers and workflow label prevent duplicate attempts and support crash recovery.
- [ ] Fresh full re-review is mandatory before closure/land.
- [ ] Only addressed findings close with remediation-head evidence; unresolved findings remain open.
- [ ] Clean non-main integration remains auto-land eligible; protected main remains human-gated.
- [ ] Partial recovery and re-escalation are durable and bounded.

### Guardrails

- Keep edits limited to `src/workflows/work-on.ts`, `src/adapters/github-workflow.ts` only if required by the lifecycle seam, and focused tests.
- Do not commit Forge runtime files or alter generated state artifacts.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

The controller already receives the completed child result in `#finalize`, can locate the existing PR with `findPullRequest`, can publish finding issues, and can resume the existing child through `SubagentsRpcClient.resume`. `GitHubIssueProjector.postArtifact` and `GitHubWorkflowAdapter.postPullArtifact` are idempotent marker-backed writes. The implementation will build on those seams rather than adding a new workflow or changing parent merge authority.

The remediation state will be represented by deterministic PR/source-issue markers and the persisted `ActiveRunLink` fields `remediationAttempts`, `remediationSourceHeadSha`, and `remediationCommitSha` (with normalization for older links). Authoritative finding parsing will consume the existing rendered issue fields (`Source PR`, `Finding ID`, confidence, severity, category, file, line, problem/evidence) and choose one open issue per PR/finding deterministically.

### Files and Responsibilities

| Path | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Finding parsing/classification, marker state, bounded resume, workflow transition, closure/re-escalation artifacts, and controller integration. |
| `test/workflows/review-findings.test.ts` | Finding issue authority, deduplication, classification, partial recovery, and closure helper coverage. |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Pure marker/classification/gate policy coverage. |

### Compatibility

Existing marker strings, result schema, review rounds, branch identity, and parent-owned merge behavior remain compatible. Older session links default new remediation fields to safe empty values.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

## Implementation Plan

1. Add strict parsing/types for linked open review-finding issues and deterministic deduplication scoped to the current PR.
2. Add pure classification and marker-state helpers. Classify low-confidence, policy/product/billing/production-safety, and explicit security-authority findings as escalation; classify only evidenced contract-safe findings as fixable.
3. Extend `ActiveRunLink` normalization with source/commit heads and read PR/source-issue comments before dispatch. Reconcile markers into the link so a crashed attempt resumes attempt 1 rather than starting another.
4. Update remediation dispatch to use authoritative issue inputs, set `workflow:in-review`, post idempotent PR+issue start markers, resume the existing child with the issue bodies/IDs, and stop when no fixable finding exists or an attempt is already complete.
5. On fresh re-review, verify the head advanced and all required reviewers completed before closing absent finding issues. Add commit-bearing closure markers and close read-back safely; preserve unresolved issues.
6. Emit completion/re-escalation artifacts on both surfaces, keep existing parent gate/auto-land semantics, and add tests for normal, partial, and policy-blocked paths.
7. Inspect the final diff, create the implementation commit, prepare the existing PR, and run the required fresh correctness/security review panel.

### Approach

The remediation path now treats open, PR-linked `review-finding` issues as authoritative data. It deduplicates them deterministically, classifies contract-safe findings separately from policy/product/security-authority escalations, and bounds remediation to one idempotent attempt on the existing child, branch, and PR.

### Changes

- Added strict finding-issue parsing, PR scoping, deterministic deduplication, and classification helpers.
- Added PR/source-issue remediation start/completion markers with partial-recovery reconciliation and `workflow:in-review` transition.
- Passed structured authoritative finding inputs to the resumed child without treating issue prose as instructions.
- Required a changed head and complete fresh reviewer roster before finding closure; closure comments include the remediation commit/head and are retry-safe.
- Preserved unresolved/policy findings and emitted durable re-escalation or clean re-review artifacts on both PR and issue.
- Added focused tests for authoritative inputs, policy classification, marker recovery, candidate gating, and idempotent finding closure.

- [x] Fresh full review is required before closure or parent-owned merge/auto-land.
- [x] Addressed findings close with commit evidence; unresolved findings remain open.
- [x] Existing parent policy preserves non-main auto-land and human-gates protected main.
- [x] Partial recovery, re-escalation, and finding closure are covered by tests.
